stated: Champion the Human Rights Act and resist any attempts to weaken or repeal it. Upholding the UK’s commitment to the European Convention on Human Rights and resisting any attempts to withdraw from it.

source.quote: Champion the Human Rights Act and resist any attempts to weaken or repeal it. Upholding the UK’s commitment to the European Convention on Human Rights and resisting any attempts to withdraw from it.

bearing_set.reason: Directly concerns the legal framework protecting civil liberties, due process, equal treatment, and democratic rights — the Human Rights Act and ECHR are the core legal-rights instruments in scope for O9.

The HRA incorporates ECHR rights to privacy (Art.8), free expression (Art.10), freedom from arbitrary detention (Art.5), and bodily autonomy — resisting weakening directly improves personal liberty and free speech protections.

membership_note: The policy is purely a rights-framework commitment; its effects fall cleanly and substantially on both the equal-treatment/due-process half (O9) and the negative-liberty/speech/privacy half (O10) of the rights taxonomy — these are the two fundamentals the HRA was designed to operationalise in domestic law.
